subject: Private control plane — IdP & SCIM integration runbook / test plan
messages:
From: Beth Carter <beth.carter@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Identity Team <identity@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Private control plane - IdP/SCIM integration details

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're kicking off the private deployment prep for the control plane that will run in our VPC/on-prem colo. Before the security review next Thursday, the identity team asked for a concise list of integration expectations so we can align our IdP (Okta) and provisioning flow:

- SAML metadata (SP metadata or ACS/Entity ID you expect)
- Required SAML attributes/claims (email, sub, role, groups, mfa) and expected claim names
- SCIM provisioning endpoint + bearer header format; exact user schema we will push (displayName, givenName, familyName, emails, groups)
- Guidance on IAM role binding for the control plane control-plane service accounts and any short-lived cert exchange (we use AWS STS for role assumption)
- Certificate rotation cadence and what to expect for downtime or rekey windows
- Any network restrictions for IdP -> control plane callbacks (allowed IP ranges, egress requirements)

Attached is our internal SSO requirements doc for context (acme-sso-requirements.pdf). Can your team produce a short runbook and a test plan we can run in our staging VPC? Ideally the runbook would include a SCIM mapping sample and a minimal SAML metadata file so our IdP team can configure a test connector.

Thanks — happy to set up a 30m call if that helps.

Beth
Beth Carter
Head of Identity Engineering, ACME Corp
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Beth Carter <beth.carter@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private control plane - IdP/SCIM integration details

Hi Beth — thanks for the context and the attachment.

High level: we support SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SSO, SCIM v2 provisioning (bearer token auth), and a role-mapping layer that can map SAML claims or SCIM group membership into control-plane RBAC roles. We've sketched a runbook and a checklist (attached) to get you to a working end-to-end test. Key bullets:

- SAML: Provide either IdP metadata or set these fields in the console: ACS URL = https://controlplane-<tenant>.redwood.local/saml/acs, Entity ID = urn:redwood:private:controlplane:<tenant>
- Required assertions: subject (NameID/email), email (email), groups (optional, multi-valued claim 'groups'), amr/mfa if available (we check for presence for elevated roles)
- SCIM: Endpoint = https://controlplane-<tenant>.redwood.local/scim/v2, Bearer token (we issue a provisioning token you upload into Okta for push provisioning)
- IAM mapping: For on-prem VPC deployments we expect the customer to map our service principal to a constrained role or service account. We provide a JSON role-mapping manifest mapping SAML Role/RoleSessionName -> control-plane service account.
- Certificate rotation: We support hot-reload for certs; recommended cadence 90 days. Rotation steps are in the runbook.

I've attached: redwood-private-idp-integration-runbook-draft.pdf and a saml-requirements-checklist.csv for your IdP team to validate. Happy to run through line-by-line on a call tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Product, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2026 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: technical notes - ACME SCIM mappings and SAML roles

Marissa / Lauren — internal notes for the runbook before we share back to ACME. Paste below the technical snippets I want in the final doc.

1) SCIM schema mapping (we should include explicit example CSV or Excel):
- userName -> emails[0].value (primary)
- name.givenName -> givenName
- name.familyName -> familyName
- displayName -> displayName
- active -> active
- externalId -> customer_id (if provided)
- groups -> groupMembership (we map groups to RBAC)

2) SAML role mapping example:
- SAML attribute 'https://redwood.com/role' -> control-plane role (admin, ops, viewer)
- If group claim present, prefer groups mapping for bulk grants
- We will generate a signed short-lived session certificate for the control-plane agent when role mapping yields admin access. This cert is rotated every 24 hours in staging by default.

3) Network notes:
- IdP callback IPs: if customer restricts egress, allow 52.23.45.0/24 and 34.199.10.0/24 (Redwood control-plane egress for SAML/SCIM)
- SCIM handshake requires outbound TLS 1.2+ and SNI with the customer hostname

4) Testing plan: create a provisioning test user 'scim-test-01@acme.com', confirm SCIM create -> user in control plane, confirm group push updates, confirm SAML sign-in with a test admin user and assert 'amr' or 'authnContext' presence.

Notes: Need to confirm whether ACME wants SCIM PATCH or only PUT for updates (Okta supports PATCH). Also need exact EntityID they will set; we'll accept metadata.xml if they POST it.

- Dev
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Beth Carter <beth.carter@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2026 13:10:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Private control plane - IdP/SCIM integration details

Beth — forwarding our internal technical notes and an updated draft runbook. See the attached files: scim-mapping.xlsx (explicit mapping table), saml-metadata.xml (sample SP metadata you can upload if you prefer metadata import), and redwood-private-iam-runbook-v1.pdf (includes step-by-step test plan).

Quick summary of changes since my earlier note:
- We included explicit SCIM attribute mappings and a preferred patch/update flow (PATCH supported; prefer incremental updates)
- We added IP ranges for egress requirements and a small troubleshooting checklist for TLS/SNI issues
- Added a pre-test checklist:
  - Create SCIM test user scim-test-01@acme.com in Okta
  - Configure a temporary provisioning token in our staging console (we will generate and share)
  - Upload either your IdP metadata XML or set these fields manually: ACS URL and Entity ID (see runbook)

If this looks good, can we lock a 45m window Wednesday morning to drive the run? Marissa / Dev will join to help configure and observe logs.
